Review_Text: A lot is made of this being a ‘must-do’ in Marrakech. I disagree. I feel it is more a ‘can-do’ if you are bored walking the endless Medina. The 30-minute lines to buy a ticket seem to be always there, and you only get shade about half the time. The garden itself is honestly just meh. Very crowded, with at least 10-20 people in line to get a picture at specific spots. The plants are all desert varieties of palm trees and cacti from all over the world, but unless you are a serious succulent geek, they are just spiny plants. There is a Koi pond with about 10 fish. You walk this crowded cement walkway around the garden and then you’re out. There is a Berber museum inside the garden which costs an extra 10 and I skipped. Bottom line, some nice benches in the shade to sit at for a lot of money and after a long line.

Review_Text: In my opinion, this is a complete rip-off. The gardens are indeed, very beautiful but very small. For a considerably less money you can see equally beautiful gardens of the Jardin Secret. Oh, you can go to one of the many beautiful parks and gardens that are carefully curated by the city and are completely free to get in. For example, crypto Park, which, despite its name is utterly delightful. The number of tourists allowed on each visit to Jardin Majorelle detract from the experience. On the day I visited I had paid both for a visit to the gardens and also to the museum. I was part of the last visit of the day, but no one told me on entrance that I needed to be at the Museum door before 4:30 pm. There was a huge group of Spanish tourists, who not only blocked pathways, slowing down the floor around the gardens, but also took up the museum. Ali visit allocation of 30 people. At 4:30 pm I was at the Museum door, but was told there were no more visits that day. I didn’t get a refund or even an apology! As advised by the workers, I contacted the Directa by telephone. Despite kindly impolitely explaining my disappointment and requesting a refund, they put the phone down on me. My recommendation is, save your money and go to one of the alternatives.

Review_Text: At the time of writing this is rated as the 12th best sight in Marrakech (out of 131). All I can say is that doesn't bode very well for the "attractions" much further down the list. The so-called Secret Garden consists of two connected rectangular gardens in the middle of the city. It's certainly nice that this was created where derelict buildings used to stand. But there really is nothing to it. It takes about five minutes to walk around, and then you wait about 10 minutes to be taken up a tower by a guide to see a view of the rooftops. But the tower isn't very high and the view isn't very interesting. If this were in London or Paris, it wouldn't even merit a footnote in one of the tourist guides. Review_Text: One of my favourite things to do in Marrakech, Le Jardin Secret is well worth the entry fee and if there had been more time I would have gone back. It was beautiful, a total escape from the busy streets outside. It felt like a really special retreat, with beautiful planting and landscaping. Unlike Majorelle Gardens which is very busy and really just full of people queuing for instagram posts, Le Jardin Secret is quiet enough to really enjoy the gardens. There is a heavily planted section that you enter through, and this transitions to a much more structured section with the same few plants repeated with precision. We unfortunately didn't stay for lunch but wish we had been able to. Highly recommend making time for this, it will give you a welcome break away from the heat and chaos of the medina. It's a really enchanting place, instantly fell in love with it!

Title: Lisamac172
Review_Text: Visited this place as was recommended by a friend and the hotel we stayed in. We took a shuttle bus from the hotel. We presumed we’d be dropped around the square, we were dropped off ( I guess where the drivers friends had taxis) we were  given no directions as to where we needed to go,  and was hassled to take a taxi. There were 2 other couples from our hotel, they got directions up on their phone , took about ten minutes to walk there, with them. We arrived later in the afternoon, as was told you need to see the square during the day and night time . As the atmosphere apparently is amazing ! Well I wouldn’t go that far, first thing we witnessed was the snakes and his charmer , the snakes were sat up even when music wasn’t played, monkeys chained up around their necks, on metal leads, they  were pulled back when they wanted to walk, some of the monkeys were pulling back on the leads , one was dressed in a football kit, one in a tuxedo and another in a dress! With cages the size of a cat carrier! Was so sad to see! Mopeds/motor cycles coming from every direction, even down little side alleys, speeding pass you. Very dangerous ! Lots of fruit juice stalls, and women offering henna tattoos, numerous people walking around with cases of sunglasses. The shops and stalls sold exactly the same things, hand bags, football shirts, cheap bracelets  You’d get hassled as soon as they saw you! Within the hour we left wasn’t staying around to see the square at night! On the  way to find a taxi, there were so many horses standing around waiting for people to get on their carriages, they all looked underweight, majority of them stood with a foot up! Every person with their horses begging us to have a ride 150 Dhm for an hour , around £10 for an hour ! Declined them all, I wasn’t paying for the poor horses to ride me around for an hour in the heat ! We went to find a taxi, 2 people asking for us to get into their taxi, we said no thanks and went to the person who was sitting in their taxi, was alot cheaper, as we went to get In the taxi , one of the other drivers was blocking the door so we couldn’t get in , because he wanted us to get in his taxi for more money . On the way back to the hotel in the taxi, see a thin donkey, tied up to a wall. Looked like he couldn’t even stand properly was leaning against the wall with his mouth wide open, wasn’t even sure it was alive !! I wouldn’t recommend visiting ! Was not enjoyable what so ever !
